title: CRISPR perturbation signatures in Alzheimer's single-cell RNA-seq

manuscript.abstract: We evaluate CRISPR perturbation effects across single-cell RNA-seq profiles to identify disease-relevant regulatory programs.
claims: CRISPR perturbation separates microglial activation states
The proposed marker panel improves disease-state clustering
The pipeline is reproducible across two donor cohorts
methods: Cluster cells with Leiden community detection
Score perturbation signatures using marker enrichment
limitations: The validation cohort is small for late-stage Alzheimer's donors
CRISPR off-target effects require additional replication
manuscript.ethicsStatement: All donor samples use de-identified consented data from public repositories.
manuscript.dataAvailability: Raw count matrices and processed annotations are listed in data/manifest.tsv.

corpusSignals.topic: CRISPR off-target replication in neurodegenerative single-cell studies
corpusSignals.rationale: Multiple papers cite off-target effects as a blocker but few replicate perturbations across donors.

corpusSignals.topic: Alzheimer microglia marker panels across public donor cohorts
corpusSignals.rationale: Fast-growing citations but limited cross-cohort marker agreement.

corpusSignals.topic: Benchmarking notebook reproducibility for disease atlas projects
corpusSignals.rationale: Notebook-based atlas projects often lack deterministic output comparisons.
